findings.title: JWT weakness (weak-secret) on GET /books/v1/{book_title}
findings.description: The JWT signing secret is guessable ('random'); an attacker can forge tokens for any user (including admins).
findings.remediation: Use a long, random, secret signing key; pin the accepted algorithm (reject 'none'); require and verify a signature and the exp claim.

findings.title: SQL injection in path parameter 'username'
findings.description: Injecting "name1' UNION SELECT NULL, username, password FROM users--" into the path parameter 'username' of GET /users/v1/{username} triggered a SQL error signature ('sqlite3'). The input reaches a SQL query without proper parameterization.
findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries or an ORM binding; never concatenate user input into SQL.

findings.title: Missing security response headers
findings.description: Responses are missing security headers: x-content-type-options, x-frame-options, content-security-policy, strict-transport-security, referrer-policy.
findings.remediation: Set X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, a CSP, HSTS, and Referrer-Policy.

findings.title: No rate limiting on GET /

findings.remediation: Enforce per-client rate limits and return 429 when exceeded.
